Elena (People Ops): Heads up: new short-term Travel Insurance Top-Up + PTO stacking option for employees travelling with immediate family on work trips. Please skim then read the linked FAQ. :memo:
Elena (People Ops): TL;DR: If youre adding a spouse/child to a company trip for up to 10 extra days, you can request a company-subsidized insurance top-up and elect PTO stacking so your schedule and benefits stay intact. Full policy below.
Elena (People Ops): Why: several people combined work travel with family visits and ran into visa/insurance gaps or had to use emergency unpaid leave. This reduces risk and makes approvals predictable.
Elena (People Ops): Key points: 1) Eligibility: immediate family (spouse/partner, dependent children) joining a business trip. 2) Top-up covers medical/evacuation for accompanying family for the trip period + up to 10 extra days. Company pays 50% of the top-up; employee pays remaining 50% via payroll deduction. 3) PTO stacking: you can split those extra days into PTO or unpaid days; managers may authorize "stacked PTO" to preserve parental leave rounding (see examples).
Elena (People Ops): How to apply: Submit the "Family Travel Add-On" form at https://redwood-internal/hr/family-travel within 7 days of booking. Manager approval required + HR confirms insurance vendor quote. Expect 3 business days for processing.
Marco: Does this affect visa letters or invite docs we already get?
Elena (People Ops): Nope. Visa letters unchanged. If the family member needs a separate visa/letter, add details on the form and HR will issue the supporting doc.
Jenna: Can contractors use this? I have a long-term contractor interviewing on-site with partner tagging along.
Elena (People Ops): Contractors are not eligible for top-up. Recruiting or vendor exceptions can be requested via case by case; recruiting ops will handle interviews with partner travel separately.
Leo: Quick payroll Q: if company covers 50% via payroll deduction how is that charged? One-time deduction?
Elena (People Ops): One-time post-trip payroll deduction labeled TRV_TOPUP on the next pay cycle. We will include an expense line in Workday for visibility.
HR Bot: Automated checklist: 1) Complete Family Travel Add-On form 2) Upload booking confirmations and family passport name(s) 3) Manager approval 4) HR confirms vendor quote 5) Payroll deduction scheduled (if applicable) 6) Upload receipts within 14 days. Form: https://redwood-internal/hr/family-travel/checklist
Ravi: Are there limits if the family member is over 65 or has pre-existing conditions?
Elena (People Ops): Insurance vendors evaluate medical risk. Pre-existing conditions may require a higher top-up or may be excluded. Please flag medical conditions on the form; HR will return vendor guidance.
Jenna: If Im combining vacation after a work trip (extra 10 days), can I use Flexible PTO and keep health benefits intact?
Elena (People Ops): Yes you can use Flexible PTO for the days youre off but on the same trip; benefits remain active for the duration of your employment. If youre gone longer than 30 days total, check with Benefits for potential coverage gaps.
Marco: Any tax implications I should be aware of?
Elena (People Ops): The company-paid portion of the insurance top-up is considered a de minimis benefit and not taxable in most jurisdictions, but exceptions exist. Benefits will send a short note to affected employees after approval.
Leo: Can managers pre-approve these proactively for recurring conferences?
Elena (People Ops): Yes. For recurring events, managers can grant a standing pre-approval for specific employees; log it in the form and HR will track annual spend.
Elena (People Ops): We'll run a 30-minute Q&A next Fri 9am PT. Calendar invite posted to #people-ops. If you have edge cases DM me. Thanks!
